title: Verbs + Prepositions
description: Master fixed verb+preposition combinations: pensar en, salir con, depender de, soñar con.

grammar.title: Verbs + Prepositions (Verbos + Preposiciones)
grammar.content:
Many Spanish verbs require a specific preposition before the next verb or noun. Unlike English, where prepositions are often intuitive, Spanish verbs lock onto their prepositions rigidly.

Most important A2.2 verb+preposition combinations:
- pensar EN (to think about) — 'Pienso en mi futuro.' (I'm thinking about my future.)
- salir CON (to go out with / to date) — 'Ella sale con su novio.' (She goes out with her boyfriend.)
- empezar A (to start to) — 'Empieza a llover.' (It starts to rain.)
- soñar CON/EN (to dream about) — 'Sueño con viajar a Japón.' (I dream of traveling to Japan.)
- depender DE (to depend on) — 'Depende de ti.' (It depends on you.)
- llamar A (to call) — 'Llamo a mi madre.' (I call my mother.)
- acabar de (to have just) — 'Acabo de llegar.' (I just arrived.)
- aprender A (to learn to) — 'Aprendo a cocinar.' (I'm learning to cook.)
- ayudar A (to help) — 'Ayudo a mi madre.' (I help my mother.)
- creer EN (to believe in) — 'Creo en la paz.' (I believe in peace.)
- olvidarse DE (to forget about) — 'Se olvida de todo.' (He/She forgets about everything.)
examples: ¿Con quién piensas ir al cine? (Who are you thinking of going to the cinema with?)
Siempre pienso en mis vacaciones. (I'm always thinking about my vacation.)
Ella sale con un chico de la clase. (She's going out with a guy from class.)
¿Con quién sueñas? (Who do you dream about?)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian also uses verb+preposition combinations, but the pairings are often different. For example, Romanian 'a gândi LA' (think at) vs Spanish 'pensar EN'. There's no reliable cross-language mapping — each verb+preposition pair must be memorized individually. However, Romanian speakers should note that Spanish prepositions (en, con, a, de) are the same words used in Romanian.

exercises.question: What preposition follows 'pensar' when meaning 'to think about'?
exercises.explanation: 'Pensar en' means 'to think about.' 'Pienso en ti' = I think about you.

exercises.question: What does 'salir con' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Salir con' means 'to go out with' or 'to date.' 'Ella sale con un chico' = She is dating a guy.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Siempre pienso ____ mis vacaciones.' (I always think about my vacation.)
exercises.explanation: 'Pienso en' — pensar requires the preposition 'en' when meaning 'to think about.'

exercises.question: What does 'acabar de + infinitive' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Acabar de + infinitive' means 'to have just done something': Acabo de llegar = I just arrived.

exercises.question: Which verb requires the preposition 'de' after it?
exercises.explanation: 'Depender de' = to depend on. 'Depende de ti' = It depends on you.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Empieza ____ llover.' (It starts to rain.)
exercises.explanation: 'Empieza a llover' — empezar requires the preposition 'a' before another verb.
